title: In-Memory Computing with Domain Wall Memory
description: An in-memory computing architecture for domain wall (racetrack) memory that computes directly on stored data, cutting the data movement between memory and processor that dominates energy in machine learning workloads.
highlights: Uses multi-domain magnetic tunnel junction reads to evaluate several stored operands in a single memory access.
Reduces many operands to one result in peripheral CMOS logic, without writing intermediate results back into the racetrack.
Supports addition, multiplication, and multiply-accumulate on shared reduction hardware, targeting neural network inference.
Evaluated from circuit to system: LTSpice for cell-level energy and latency, NVSim for array-level cost, and RTSim for end-to-end workloads.

title: Vehicle Lane-Change Prediction
description: My Master's project at Penn State: a hybrid LSTM-HMM model that predicts whether a vehicle will change lanes left, keep its lane, or change lanes right from its recent trajectory, evaluated on the NGSIM highway dataset.
highlights: Pairs a hidden Markov model with an LSTM that produces its emission probabilities, so the HMM captures maneuver phases while the LSTM learns features from the raw trajectory.
Trains one model per maneuver and classifies a trajectory by which model assigns it the highest likelihood, computed with the forward algorithm in log space.
Outperformed standalone LSTM and neural-emission HMM baselines trained on the same data.

title: Skin Infection Detection
description: A real-time skin infection detection app that classifies photos of affected skin, supporting early diagnosis and reducing reliance on in-person consultations.
highlights: Built and deployed with a distributed full-stack architecture: an Android client, Flask and Node.js services, and a PostgreSQL database, containerized with Docker.
Runs image classification on-device for real-time results.

title: AI Skincare Advisor
description: My final year project at HKU: a mobile app that scores a user's skin concerns from a selfie and recommends skincare products suited to them.
highlights: Built a computer vision pipeline that locates facial landmarks, then scores acne, wrinkles and crow's feet, dark eye circles, sallowness, and skin tone, alongside age and gender estimation.
Recommends products from a catalogue compiled from Sephora's website, matching the skin scores and the user's text input with NLP techniques.
Served the pipeline through a Flask API consumed by a React Native mobile app.

title: Web-Based Chat Application
description: A real-time chat system where multiple users can send messages simultaneously, with conversations updating automatically.
